When we add the acid to the water, ΔPH will be negative:
When we add an acid to the water, the water acidity will increase, then [H⁺] increase and PH decrease so ΔPH = −

Inversely proportional: PH, [H⁺]; [H⁺], [OH⁻]

Decomposition degree of HNO₂ increase by adding water while it’s decrease
by adding KNO₂ to it

the decomposition degree of HNO₂ increased because Dilution decreases the amount of the
dissolved substance per volume unit. To remove this effect, according to Lechatlier principle,
the dissolved substance decomposes even further. Thus the ratio of the dissolved to the new
volume unit increases. Therefore the decomposition degree increases.
WHILE by adding KNO₂ the degree of ionization decrease ,This is because of the composition of
the common ion which leads to an increase of the rate of the converse reaction according to
LeChatilier principle. Thus, [H⁺] decreases causing a decrease of acidity and a decrease in the
acid's degree of ionization.

KNO₂ → K⁺ + NO₂⁻

a:
احنا متفقين على ان المادة الثالثة المضافة (سواء جانت حامض قوي اوو قاعدة قوية) لازم تكون قيمتها اللي راح تتعوض بقوانين بفر فقط تركيز مولاري M.
بس ممكن تعطى بالسؤال باكثررر من شكل و بالاخير لازم مثل متفقنا لازم تتحول الى تركيز مولاري (و اكيد اذا اكو حجمين بالسؤال فلازم نسوي عملية تخفيف).

ممكن مباشرة تعطى M تركيز مولاري مثل سؤال صفحة 76.

q: Solubility Product constant Ksp
a:
This value remains constant at a certain temperature. Solubility product constant is used to express
(or measure) the solubility of slightly soluble salts in water. The solubility of a compound is directly
proportional to its solubility product. Generally, the solubility product of a slightly soluble ionic
compound is calculated through the molar concentrations of ions making up of the compound at
equilibrium (in saturated solutions molar solubility is shown with-s-). When writing solubility
product constant in equilibrium chemical equation, the concentrations of ions formed from
decomposition of compounds are multiplied. Mole numbers are written as exponents

because the addition of acid (increase in H+ ion
concentration) causes H+ ions to combine with

the equilibrium of the compound. To compensate

for the decrease in OH− ions, more Mg(OH)2
dissociates, leading to an increase in its solubility

q: Find the pOH value of 0.5 M aqueous solution of ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃: (pKb = 4.74)
a:
PH = ½(PKw − PKb − log [salt])
PH = ½(14 − 4.74 − log 5 × 10⁻¹)
PH = ½(14 − 4.74 + 1 − 0.7)
PH = 9.56/2 = 4.78
∴ POH = 14 − 4.78 ⇒ POH = 9.22
